result.verdict: Request changes. The direction is right: one canonical export, a consumer-only manifest, and fence-driven data checks. But three things should block merge. The change removes a link check on a file that still ships in the package, it leaves an existing repo check failing, and it may break the diagnostic page tables. The data package README is also written as a release-candidate note, not canonical consumer docs. The data reference mostly matches the supplied text and assertions, apart from a few unstated behaviors listed below. Most of the test removals replace obsolete corpus checks, but two useful checks were lost: dependency-closure for the skill scripts, and a guard that every reference fence is executed.
blockingIssues: stage-package.mjs no longer checks links in upgradeGuide.md, but package.json `files` (and package.test's expected list) still ship it. It very likely links to the retired pages (typescript.md, radio.md, events.class.md, optional-backbone.md). Removing the check hides broken links in the npm tarball. Either fix upgradeGuide links to point at canonical pages or rewrite it, and restore the check. Or drop upgradeGuide.md from `files` and state that decision.

`npm run check:api-contracts` fails because docs/typescript.md was removed. Merging a check you know is red is a regression, whether or not anyone claims green CI. Before merge, point it at the new pages or explicitly retire or skip it, with a tracked issue.

build.mjs diagnosticPage: the Benchmark row was removed and `${replacement}` now sits on its own line after the table. If `replacement` starts with `\n| Replacement… |` (it used to follow the row directly), the output gets a blank line that ends the table, so the replacement row renders as a separate broken block. Fix it as `| Surfaces | ${surfaces}${historical} |${replacement}`. Also check the output for one historical and one replaced diagnostic. The passing 41-entry catalog check probably doesn't render Markdown tables.

packages/data/readme.md ships in the @mnjs/data npm package, but it describes release-candidate process: 'rebuilt 5.0.0-rc.2 candidate', 'registry package ... not verified', installing `./artifacts/*.tgz`. After publication that text is wrong for every registry user, and it hardcodes a version that will drift. Canonical docs should say `npm install @mnjs/data` (plus marionette for integration). Candidate-tarball instructions belong only in START-HERE.md or release evidence.
risks: Starter allowScripts regression: the old package.mjs set `allowScripts['marionette@<version>'] = false`. buildDevelopmentKit rewrites only `dependencies`, so that entry is gone unless the fixture's package.json already has it for rc.2. Check the generated starter/package.json, or add the entry in buildDevelopmentKit.

skills/marionette/scripts/symbols.mjs still ships, but docs-symbols.json no longer exists. If docs.mjs imports or reads the symbol index at startup, or while verifying the manifest, `--list`/`--search` could fail in an installed package. The generic lookup is tested in-repo; the packed-install path for the helper is unverified.
`node -p "require.resolve('marionette/package.json')"` in agents.md and SKILL.md throws ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED unless `exports` includes './package.json'. Unverified from the supplied context.

Interim coverage regression: the Radio, Backbone adapter, events.class, TypeScript, and utils pages were deleted from the shipped docs. The @mnjs/data README still tells users to install @mnjs/radio. Acceptable for a bounded slice only if docs/api.md clearly lists the missing families. That claim is unverified.

The consumer package now ships examples/records/scripts/build-local-packages.mjs, package-lock.json, and public/api fixtures. That is repo dev tooling and records-specific scaffolding inside a framework-wide package. It also conflicts with the goal of staying independent of the records example, and export.test now hard-requires records assets.

data-reference-checks keys assertions by position (data-1..3). Adding or reordering a fence in data.md moves every assertion onto a different fence, which fails confusingly or, worse, passes against the wrong fence.

buildDevelopmentKit's default `readdir(source)` fallback would pick up directories and node_modules, and readRegularFile throws on those. `mkdir(destination)` without `recursive` assumes artifactDir already exists.

DataApi `serialize` returns live attributes, while the docs present toObject/toArray as copies. Templates that mutate data will silently mutate the Model with no events. It is documented, but easy to miss.
incorrectAssumptions: It is incorrect that removing the upgradeGuide link check is part of retiring the corpus. The file still ships, so the check still guards consumer-visible content.

The package.mjs prefix filters (benchmarks/, config/api-contracts/, test/unit/ ...) were removed on the assumption that resources.json alone keeps the manifest clean. The new test guards only the planning|benchmarks|test prefixes. config/, scripts/, and repo-root files can now enter the package with no guard.
'Destroy prevents subsequent data mutations' does not say whether a mutation after destroy throws or silently does nothing. The data-1 assertion relies on a silent no-op. State that in data.md.

The docs don't say whether destroying a Model emits `remove` and `update` on each containing Collection before `destroy` is forwarded. The ordering correction already in progress should also cover these events.
The claim that ESM and CommonJS `require('@mnjs/data')` have matching declarations has no supplied test behind it.
missingTests: Dependency closure for the skill: export.test now follows only examples/records/src imports. Add skills/marionette/scripts/*.mjs to the module queue so docs.mjs → search.mjs/symbols.mjs imports are proven to be exported.

Packed-install smoke test that runs the documented commands exactly: `require.resolve('marionette/package.json')`, and `docs.mjs --list`, `--search 'prepareStart'`, `--page docs/api/application.md`, `--section <id>` against node_modules, with no docs-symbols.json present.
A completeness guard for the reference runner: every js/ts fence in canonical pages is either executed or explicitly exempted, and IDs are stable (anchored to headings or markers, not position).
A rendered-Markdown check for diagnostic pages with and without `replacement`: the table must parse as a single table.
Link validation over every shipped Markdown file (readme.md, upgradeGuide.md, docs/**, examples/records/README.md, skills/**/SKILL.md), not only pages from the manifest.
Starter output test: the generated package.json has the expected dependencies and allowScripts, and the file inventory equals sourceFiles plus package-lock.json.

Data: a mutation after destroy (throws or no-op, whichever is the contract), Model destroy → Collection remove/update/destroy event order, a CJS require smoke test with a types check, and the subscribe event-map overload including idempotent cleanup.
simplifications: Make `sourceFiles` required in buildDevelopmentKit and delete the readdir fallback. Better still, keep the list in the fixture (e.g. a files.json) rather than inline in build-artifact.mjs.
Drop symbols.mjs from resources.json and the skill until the mappings are correct, rather than shipping a dead helper that is only 'unadvertised'.
Ship only the records example's src/, README, index.html, and package.json. Leave out the lockfile, the build-local-packages script, and the Playwright spec, or link to the repo instead.
Collapse the two identical `npm install ./artifacts/*.tgz` blocks in the data README into a single registry install line.
agents.md and SKILL.md duplicate the route table, which the generator keeps in sync. Fine to keep, but SKILL.md could just point to docs/agents.md and drop its own 'Apply the contract' prose.
nextSteps: Fix the diagnosticPage table join and check the rendered output.
Resolve upgradeGuide.md (fix its links or stop shipping it) and restore its link check.
Retarget or formally retire check:api-contracts so the repo checks are green or the exemption is explicit.
Rewrite packages/data/readme.md for registry users and move the candidate wording to START-HERE.md.
Check starter allowScripts and the packed-install behavior of the helper and require.resolve. Add the missing closure, fence-completeness, and link tests.

Apply the pending data corrections (subscribe event map, destroy ordering), plus the post-destroy mutation semantics, then run the full build, docs:check, and fresh packed install before claiming the slice is done.
